title: Calculating the Corrective Entry on a Personal Checking Account
content:
The corrective entry is the charges under review less the charge the schedule produces, never below zero.

Every overdraft-item charge standing on the Personal Checking account counts toward the charges under review, whenever it posted.

The account is taken to carry the number of chargeable overdraft items the tier allows for one business day. Each chargeable item is charged at the tier's overdraft fee for each item. The charge the schedule produces is the charge for each chargeable item multiplied by the smaller of the number of overdraft charges standing and the number of chargeable items allowed.

The corrective entry is taken in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up.

**Worked example on hypothetical inputs.** Take an account whose tier allows 3 chargeable overdraft items for one business day and charges 35.00 for each item paid into overdraft, and on which 4 overdraft charges stand, totalling 138.00.

| Quantity | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Charges under review | 138.00 |
| Charge for each chargeable item | 35.00 |
| Number of overdraft charges standing | 4 |
| Number of chargeable items allowed | 3 |
| Charge the schedule produces | 35.00 multiplied by 3, which is 105.00 |
| Charges under review less that charge | 33.00 |
| Corrective entry, in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up | 35.00 |

The smaller of the two counts is what multiplies the per-item charge, so the fourth standing charge adds nothing to the schedule figure. Had the charges under review come to 100.00 against the same schedule figure of 105.00, the difference would fall below zero and the corrective entry would be 0.00.
